1	# Feishu Formatting and Safe-Update Rules
2	
3	## Priority
4	
5	1. Preserve facts, links, structure, and unrelated rich content.
6	2. Follow explicit user styling.
7	3. Otherwise use the expert technical-report defaults.
8	4. Stop when uniqueness, completion, or structural integrity cannot be proven.
9	
10	## Operation decision table
11	
12	| Situation | Operation | Verification |
13	|---|---|---|
14	| New short document | `create_doc`; title must not repeat as first H1 | full fetch |
15	| New long document | create first segment, ordered append; location args remain mutually exclusive | poll task then fetch each segment |
16	| Replace one fetched media-free section | `replace_range` + `selection_by_title` | section + neighbors |
17	| Restyle one table/block | unique local `replace_range` | block + neighbors |
18	| Add adjacent/end content | precise insert / true-end append | boundary/tail |
19	| Existing broad rebuild | forbidden by this safety policy: `overwrite`, `replace_all` | n/a |
20	| Non-unique selection | stop and refine from fresh fetch | uniqueness first |
21	
22	`wiki_node`, `wiki_space`, and `folder_token` are mutually exclusive on creation.
23	
24	## Fetch and manifest
25	
26	`fetch_doc` does not select by heading. By default, call it without `limit`/`offset` and fetch the complete document, then locate locally. Only when the user explicitly requests pagination may `limit`/`offset` be used; continue until the complete target block plus predecessor/successor is available. Record headings, tables, code/Mermaid fences, containers, media token/order/neighbors, and target/preserve status.
27	
28	A fetched `<whiteboard token="..."/>` is read-only evidence, not creation syntax.
29	
30	## Width policy
31	
32	**Match the document's actual text-column width** so the table neither overflows nor looks narrow. Do not assume a fixed number: verify against a rendered reference — the table must not extend past the adjacent callout/heading right edge. Feishu wide-mode docs are ≈ **900–960px (930 typical)**; classic/narrow docs are ≈ **780–820px (800 typical)**. When a rendered table overflows, reduce the total (a one-number-per-table change) rather than assuming the default. Width count = columns, widths are positive integers, and sum = chosen total.
33	
34	| Role | Typical px | Alignment |
35	|---|---:|---|
36	| index/icon/tiny enum | 70–100 | center |
37	| status/date/version | 90–140 | center |
38	| numeric/delta | 105–145 | center |
39	| symbol/API | 150–220 | usually left |
40	| repo/code path/revision | 210–300 | left |
41	| explanation/evidence/cause/procedure | 280–500 or remainder | left |
42	
43	If 960px cannot remain readable, split by reader question. Exceed 960 only when the user explicitly overrides the default. A one-off compact/equal-width/all-left request also overrides defaults without changing future defaults.
44	
45	Examples (930px):
46	- `类型/版本/说明`: `130,150,650`
47	- `状态/Change/路径/说明`: `110,140,270,410`
48	- `指标/前/后/变化/来源/解释`: `180,115,115,110,100,310`
49	
50	### Uniform-centered style (common user request)
51	
52	When the user asks for「表格总宽度 = 文本宽度、文本水平居中」or an equivalent uniform look: use **equal columns** summing to the text width and set `{align="center"}` on **every** cell (header and data). Equal-split examples — 800px: 5-col `160,160,160,160,160`, 4-col `200,200,200,200`, 3-col `266,267,267`, 2-col `400,400`; 930px: 5-col `186×5`, 4-col `232,233,232,233`, 3-col `310,310,310`.
53	
54	### Alignment
55	
56	Center headers and compact values with `{align="center"}`; center **all** cells for the uniform-centered style. Omit `align` for left-aligned paths/prose. Put attributes outside bold. Do not emit `{align="left"}`.
57	
58	**Vertical centering (垂直居中) cannot be set through the MCP/markdown update tool** — `{align=...}` controls horizontal alignment only. Vertical alignment is a table-cell property applied in the Feishu UI (select the table → cell alignment → 垂直居中). Never claim vertical centering was applied by a write; report it as a one-click UI follow-up.
59	
60	## lark-table structure
61	
62	Hierarchy is `lark-table → lark-tr → lark-td`; each row has equal cells; cell content has surrounding blank lines; do not mix pipe-table syntax or nest lark-tables.
63	
64	Enhanced cells may contain complex content such as a fenced code block when the complete nested structure is intentionally generated and validated. Keep ordinary technical-report code blocks outside tables by default for readability. Do not place Mermaid, media, or another lark-table inside a cell.
65	
66	## Bold safety
67	
68	Use paired same-block `**text**`, no inner whitespace/newline, no escaping when emphasis is intended, no split delimiters, and no changes inside code. Repair the smallest complete paragraph/list/callout/cell; never run a document-wide regex.
69	
70	## Punctuation locale consistency
71	
72	Match every punctuation mark to its surrounding language and never mix locales within one run. This applies to **all** punctuation (colon, comma, period, semicolon, enumeration comma `、`, brackets, quotes, exclamation/question marks, ellipsis, dash), not only colons.
73	
74	- CJK context (both sides CJK, or at least one adjacent side is CJK): use full-width CJK punctuation — `：，。；、！？（）【】「」《》…——` — with no trailing ASCII space.
75	- Pure Latin/ASCII context (both sides are English words, numbers, code tokens, or identifiers): use the ASCII mark followed by a single space — `: ` `, ` `; ` `. ` — never a full-width mark.
76	- Never mix inside one clause: `实测结论:即` → `实测结论：即`; `codec-only,parser` → `codec-only, parser`; a Chinese sentence must not delimit clauses with ASCII `,`/`;`, and an all-English list must not use `，`/`；`.
77	- Do not alter punctuation inside fenced code blocks or ASCII diagrams — full-width marks are wider and break monospace alignment, and code content must stay byte-exact. Normalize prose, headings, callouts, blockquotes, and table cells only.
78	- When normalizing, edit the smallest unique block and reproduce the surrounding text (especially comment-anchored spans) exactly, so comment anchors are not orphaned.
79	
80	## Fence and container safety
81	
82	- Preserve matching fence and language labels.
83	- A selection contains the complete fence/container or none of it.
84	- Compare fence count, language, first/last content line, and order after each batch.
85	- Keep Mermaid/code outside callouts.
86	- Mermaid conversion warnings are failures to investigate.
87	
88	## Selection safety
89	
90	- `selection_by_title` replaces the complete heading section; use only after fetching and confirming that scope.
91	- `selection_with_ellipsis` boundaries should use 10–20 unique characters.
92	- Literal `...` in source must be escaped as `\.\.\.`.
93	- `insert_after` uses the matched range end; `insert_before` uses its start.
94	- Non-unique selection is a stop condition, not a reason to broaden across media.
95	
96	## Ordered asynchronous batches
97	
98	1. Fetch the complete document by default (or user-requested pages) and build the manifest.
99	2. Number targets by current document order.
100	3. Mutate the earliest complete block.
101	4. If a `task_id` returns, poll the same tool until terminal success/failure; pending is not completion.
102	5. Fetch the complete affected block and neighbors.
103	6. Validate content, table shape/width/alignment, bold, fences, containers, media, warnings, and unrelated content.
104	7. Only after PASS mutate the next block.
105	8. Finish with a full fetch and manifest comparison.
106	
107	One section per batch is the long-report default. Split oversized sections only at heading/complete-block boundaries.
108	
109	## Red flags
110	
111	- existing-document overwrite/replace_all;
112	- pending task followed by another mutation or early fetch;
113	- non-unique or media-crossing selection;
114	- width count/sum mismatch, or an unverified fixed width that overflows/underfills the document text column;
115	- claiming vertical centering was set by a write (it is UI-only);
116	- blanket-centered path/prose;
117	- broken fence/container;
118	- next batch before read-back;
119	- changed media/fence/table count without intent;
120	- MCP acceptance treated as rendered success.
121

1	# ASCII text-sketch pattern catalog
2	
3	Reusable fenced-`plaintext` patterns for explaining code. Pick by information shape. Every label must be grounded (see SKILL.md §1). Keep width within the text column (~80–100 mono cols). Examples are illustrative skeletons — replace with real identifiers/values.
4	
5	## 1. Dispatch / fall-through flow
6	
7	Use for "try fast path, else fall back". Boxes + arrows + branch labels; put the return/condition on the edge.
8	
9	```plaintext
10	   float32 conv Eval
11	        │
12	   ┌────┴─────┐  是   ┌──────────────────┐
13	   │is_hybrid?│─────► │  ConvEvalHybrid   │
14	   └────┬─────┘       └──────────────────┘
15	       否
16	        ▼
17	   ┌────────────────────────┐  ==kHandled  ┌───────────┐
18	   │   EvalConvF32(...)      │────────────► │ break 完成 │
19	   └───────────┬────────────┘              └───────────┘
20	               │ kFallback / kCmsisError
21	               ▼
22	   ┌────────────────────────┐
23	   │   reference_ops::Conv   │  标量兜底→标量回退（去俚语）
24	   └────────────────────────┘

28	
29	Use for "all conditions must hold to continue". List the real conditions ①②③.

35	   │  ③ shape 自洽 (batch/通道/bias 数对得上)   │
36	   └──────────┬──────────────────┬────────────┘
37	        任一 ✗ │            全 ✓ │
38	              ▼                   ▼

84

108

119

123	 out[c] = Σ(x × filter_c) + bias[c]           x = [1,2,3]
124	   c0: filter0=[1, 0,-1] bias=10 → (1+0−3)+10 =  8
125	   c1: filter1=[2, 1, 0] bias=20 → (2+2+0)+20 = 24

128	   通道0 全部+10   通道1 全部+20   通道2 全部+30
129	    1→11  4→14      2→22  5→25      3→33  6→36
130	```
131	
132	## 10. Code-snippet + one-line annotation
133	
134	When the reader asks for "real code, not '无代码'", quote the actual loop/statement and annotate the single line that matters. Do not paraphrase it into prose.
135	
136	```plaintext
137	 for (batch) for (out_y) for (out_x) for (out_channel c) {
138	   int32_t acc = 0;
139	   for (fy) for (fx) for (ic) acc += filter_val*(input_val+input_offset);
140	   if (bias_data) acc += bias_data[c];   // integer_ops/conv.h:123 每个空间位置重读 bias_data[c]
141	 }
142	```
143	
144	## Comparison table — only for exact parallel values
145	
146	Use a table (or `lark-table`) when the content is genuinely parallel columns, e.g. before/after or A-vs-B. If it encodes order/causality, use a sketch instead.
147	
148	```plaintext
149	                 AllocateTempInputTensor(Prepare)   GetEvalInput(Eval)
150	 返回            TfLiteTensor*（重/信息全）           TfLiteEvalTensor*（轻）
151	 目的            读元数据→校验+算缓冲                  拿数据指针→做运算
152	 生命周期        arena 临时区，用完 Deallocate         常驻，不释放
153	```
154	
155	## Anti-patterns
156	
157	- A branch label that is a guess ("size ok?") instead of the real condition.

94a77d7 fix(notify): make Gerrit/Jira polling actually work end-to-end
The notify poller could never complete a successful poll on-device.
Five device-side defects, all verified on goldfish-arm64 emulator:

- Stack overflow: AGENT_NOTIFY_STACK was 8KB while the poll runs
  mcp_client_execute -> vela_tls HTTPS handshake on the notify
  thread's stack (NuttX pthread stacks are heap-allocated).  The
  first successful Gerrit poll overflowed into the heap and killed
  the board with a recursive assert.  Bump to 32KB; the agent loop
  does the same TLS work on 64KB.

- Wrong default jira tool name: "jira.search" never matched the
  discovered "jira.jira_search" (server-prefixed), so every jira
  poll failed before reaching the network.

- Empty error strings: mcp_client_execute returned ERROR leaving
  the output buffer untouched, so poll failures logged an empty
  reason.  Fill a JSON error string on tool/server-not-found.

- Gerrit text format unparsed: the onedev gateway's query_changes
  returns a plain-text summary ("- 123: subject") rather than a
  JSON array; gerrit_dedup only parsed JSON and silently reported
  nothing.  Add a line-scanning fallback (gerrit_scan_text).

- No self-heal: if boot-time discovery lost the race with the
  network link, the tool table stayed empty forever.  Re-discover
  once per poll when tools are missing (rate-limited by the poll
  interval).

Also: jira_search returns summary inline on each issue (no
"fields" wrapper) - accept both shapes; cap toasts at
AGENT_NOTIFY_MAX_NEW (16) per poll while still advancing the
cursor so a large backlog neither storms the UI nor re-reports.

Verified: gerrit poll returns 3 new changes, cursor dedups across
polls and reboots, zero crashes; jira rides through the current
acc.pt.miui.com gateway flap (fails with reason, auto-recovers
when the upstream returns).

本文件记录 2026-09-20 一轮 AI 主导开发（Claude Code，方向由团队对话确定）的
真实过程与运行证据：设备端 `ai_agent` 新增「PC 侧编译」腿、远程编码完成播报、

## 架构（改动后）

```
QEMU 内 ai_agent (ReAct loop,「编译 vela」builtin skill)
      │  MCP over HTTP (10.0.2.2:8760)
      ▼
remote_ctrl MCP server (PC 侧, 本轮入仓 pc/)
  tools: rc_repo_open/rc_read_file/rc_write_patch/rc_run/rc_git/rc_summary
       + vela_build / vela_build_status (新增)
      │  vela_build 起后台线程: unset CROSSDEV; envsetup && lunch && m -j20
      ▼
真实 vela 构建 out/openvela_vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/vela_ap.bin
```

- `vela_build` 只负责发起（<1 s 返回）；设备侧 HTTP 读超时 120 s
  （`AGENT_LLM_SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SEC`），编译 35 s~数分钟，同步等待必超时。
- `vela_build_status {"wait": 60}`：server 端阻塞最长 90 s（低于设备 120 s 读
  超时）。设备 LLM 无法在轮次间 sleep，`wait` 是它控制轮询节奏的唯一手段；
  一次 wait 间隔取代紧循环轮询。
- running 态回复三行、不带 log_tail；失败才附 log_tail（末 ~2.5 KB 定位错误行）。

## BK7258 板上 media 框架可行性（spike，结论 no-go）

真实工具链（armv8-m.main / cortex-m33 soft-float）实测：

| 项 | 实测 |
|----|------|
| AP 基线 | `app1.bin` 336,852 B（XIP 2.78 MB，余 2.58 MB；RAM 336 KB） |
| `CONFIG_MEDIA_SERVER=y` | 构建失败：`media_plugin.c:3` 无条件 `#include <libavutil/mem.h>`，全树无 ARMv8-M ffmpeg（prebuilts 仅 A64/x86） |
| 退到 `CONFIG_MEDIA=y`（仅 client） | 仍失败：`utils/media_utils.c:25` `#include <cutils/properties.h>`，AP 无 property 服务 |
| 还原 | defconfig 复原后构建 `decode pass`，镜像与基线逐字节一致 |

结论：media server 本身编不过，不是体积问题；板侧 `pcm0p`/`pcm0c` 维持

text:
Broker（消息代理）= 我们这条「远程编码」链路里的**消息中转服务器**，具体是一台 MQTT 服务器。两端不直连，都只连它，由它按主题（topic）把消息转投给对方：

```plaintext
设备端 ai_agent（qemu / vela）
   │  MQTT 发布/订阅（rask / 权限快照 / 审批结果 / 编码 transcript）
   ▼
MQTT broker  ←── 就是这个"中转站"：双方都是它的客户端，
   │            它负责把 A 发的消息投递给订阅了该主题的 B
   ▼
PC 侧 acp-bridge（mimo acp 真编码 / fake-adapter 假编码）
```

三个关键点：

- **作用**：邮局/群聊服务器式解耦。设备与 bridge 互相不知道对方 IP，只要都能连上同一个 broker 就能通信（也天然穿过 NAT——设备出方向连 broker 即可）。
- **我们测试时用的**：我在宿主机本机起的 `mosquitto`（localhost:1883）+ acp-bridge 的 fake-adapter——所以 toast 闭环能全通，但只算「自导自演」。
- **为什么在等它**：真机演示要用**团队统一部署的 broker 地址**（队友那边的 mimocode 环境连哪个，我们就填哪个，设备 `set_remote` 的参数就是它）。安装源和 broker 地址拿到后，把 fake-adapter 换成真 mimo acp、地址从 localhost 换成真址，链路当天可通——设备侧代码一行不用改。

1	# DeskMate ACP bridge — PC loop milestone
2	
3	The bridge is the PC-only ACP Client. It starts one backend (`mimo acp` or `kiro-cli acp`), normalizes its state, and exposes only DeskMate Link through a local Unix-domain socket or MQTT. The terminal client is an ACP-agnostic stand-in for the future OpenVela client.
4	
5	The frozen link contract is [../../docs/protocol.md](../../docs/protocol.md). The client never receives ACP session IDs, raw tool arguments, credentials, or Agent-specific extension messages.
6	
7	## Deterministic loop verification
8	
9	```sh
10	cd tools/acp-bridge
11	npm test
12	npm run demo:loop
13	```
14	
15	The fake adapter integration test proves nonce handshake, Unix socket delivery, host-side argument redaction, `ptSubmit`, exact option ID mapping, and duplicate decision suppression. It does not claim hardware or real-Agent permission control.
16	
17	## Interactive PC client
18	
19	In one terminal, start the bridge. `fake` is the deterministic loop backend:
20	
21	```sh
22	node bin/deskmate-bridge.mjs --backend fake --socket /tmp/deskmate-link.sock
23	```
24	
25	In another terminal, start the client:
26	
27	```sh
28	node bin/deskmate-client.mjs --socket /tmp/deskmate-link.sock
29	```
30	
31	The client sends hello with a fresh nonce and then displays `Offline`, `Idle`, `Busy`, `Attention`, or `Result` from DeskMate snapshots. Its commands are `status`, `once`, `deny`, `disconnect`, and `quit`. It has no `ptSubmit` command: only the bridge's ACP capture path can create a prompt.
32	
33	For the fake demo, type `prompt` into the bridge terminal. This creates a synthetic request solely for PC-loop testing; it never runs a command. Then choose `once` or `deny` in the client terminal.
34	
35	## Real ACP state-flow probe
36	
37	Use a selected backend in the bridge terminal. It provides a small shell-style
38	REPL: `deskmate>` accepts ordinary text as an ACP prompt and streams agent text,
39	tool state, permission waits, and Billing events locally while continuing to
40	publish the same facts to the DeskMate Link.
41	
42	```sh
43	node bin/deskmate-bridge.mjs --backend mimo --socket /tmp/deskmate-link.sock
44	node bin/deskmate-bridge.mjs --backend kiro --socket /tmp/deskmate-link.sock
45	```
46	
47	The local commands are `help`, `status`, `usage`, and `quit`/`exit`; all other
48	input is sent as an ACP prompt. The adapter runs `initialize`, `session/new`,
49	and `session/prompt`, then turns `session/update` tool/text activity into
50	DeskMate facts. A real `session/request_permission` is held until the terminal
51	client sends `once` or `deny`; only the Agent-provided `allow_once` or
52	`reject_once` option ID can be returned.
53	
54	## Session-local usage
55	
56	The bridge maintains an in-memory ledger for the one ACP session it creates. It publishes a `usage_snapshot` after the nonce handshake, on each observed usage increment, and every 30 seconds. The terminal client's `usage` command asks for the same snapshot without issuing a model prompt.
57	
58	- The snapshot has two display-ready `billing` slots: `charge` (left) and raw `tokens` (right). A device can render them as `Billing: <charge> / <total tokens>` and leaves any `null` slot blank.
59	- MiMoCode contributes raw `input`/`output`/`total` tokens to the right slot from a completed `session/prompt`, plus separate token-based context-window use from `usage_update`.
60	- Kiro contributes incremental `credits` to the left slot from `_kiro.dev/metadata.meteringUsage`; it does not expose raw token counts through ACP. Its context value is a percentage, not a token count.
61	- A verified provider currency amount can use the same left slot with `kind: "currency"`; the bridge does not treat MiMoCode's local `$0` estimate as a real price.
62	- The snapshot is only the bridge-process lifetime total for its current ACP session. It is never an account balance, remaining quota, rate-limit reading, or cross-machine aggregate. Units are deliberately never converted or summed together.
63	
64	Known limitation: the current MiMoCode profile has been observed to complete a bash tool call without emitting `session/request_permission`. The bridge will show its state/tool result but will not invent an Attention prompt; this is not a permission-control success.
65	
66	## Local MQTT transport
67	
68	MQTT is the wireless DeskMate Link shared by the simulator and the real board. Run Mosquitto on the PC, then start the bridge with an explicit broker, topic prefix, and device ID:
69	
70	```sh
71	mosquitto -p 18883 -v
72	node bin/deskmate-bridge.mjs --backend fake --transport mqtt \
73	  --broker mqtt://127.0.0.1:18883 --topic-prefix deskmate --device-id demo-1
74	node bin/deskmate-client.mjs --transport mqtt \
75	  --broker mqtt://127.0.0.1:18883 --topic-prefix deskmate --device-id demo-1
76	```
77	
78	The bridge subscribes to `deskmate/demo-1/device-to-bridge`, publishes to `deskmate/demo-1/bridge-to-device`, and publishes non-retained `online`/LWT `offline` status to `deskmate/demo-1/status`. MQTT uses version 5, clean start, session expiry `0`, QoS `0`, and non-retained DeskMate messages. Set `DESKMATE_MQTT_USERNAME` and `DESKMATE_MQTT_PASSWORD` only through the environment when a broker requires authentication; never put credentials in commands, fixtures, or logs.
79	
80	## Unified launcher
81	
82	`bin/deskmate-demo.sh` shortens PC validation while keeping broker, bridge, and device/client in separate terminals. It accepts the real ACP backend and link transport as positional arguments:
83	
84	```sh
85	# Terminal 1: local-only broker for PC validation
86	bin/deskmate-demo.sh broker --port 18883
87	
88	# Terminal 2: use a real ACP backend over MQTT
89	bin/deskmate-demo.sh bridge mimo mqtt --broker mqtt://127.0.0.1:18883 --device-id goldfish-1
90	# Or: bin/deskmate-demo.sh bridge kiro mqtt --broker mqtt://127.0.0.1:18883 --device-id goldfish-1
91	
92	# Terminal 3: PC device stand-in; later replace with the simulator or board
93	bin/deskmate-demo.sh client mqtt --broker mqtt://127.0.0.1:18883 --device-id goldfish-1
94	```
95	
96	### Attach the native MiMo TUI to the bridge session
97	
98	MiMo ACP exposes an attachable loopback server as well as its stdio ACP stream.
99	For a MiMo bridge, `--mimo-attach` gives the ACP server an explicit port,
100	waits until the bridge has created its actual ACP session, then opens a tmux
101	window attached to that exact session. It never guesses a session ID from logs:
102	
103	```sh
104	bin/deskmate-demo.sh bridge mimo mqtt \
105	  --broker mqtt://10.189.140.244:1883 --device-id goldfish-1 \
106	  --mimo-attach --mimo-attach-port 4096
107	```
108	
109	The chosen port must be unused before launch. If an earlier `mimo acp` still
110	owns `4096`, stop that bridge first or choose another explicit port, such as
111	`--mimo-attach-port 4097`.
112	
113	The bridge writes an atomic, mode-`0600` runtime ready file containing only the
114	loopback URL and session ID, then deletes it when the bridge exits. Inside tmux,
115	the launcher creates a `deskmate-mimo` window running `mimo attach`. Outside
116	tmux, it opens a GNOME Terminal by default. It prints the exact attach command
117	only when no graphical session is available, `gnome-terminal` is unavailable,
118	or launching it fails. The native TUI and DeskMate share one ACP session: do
119	not submit concurrent prompts from the TUI, `deskmate>`, and device `@` input.
120	
121	For the existing loop transport, replace the two final commands with `bridge <backend> loop` and `client loop`. Run `bin/deskmate-demo.sh --help` for all parameters. The launcher reads MQTT credentials only from `DESKMATE_MQTT_USERNAME` and `DESKMATE_MQTT_PASSWORD`.
122	# DeskMate ACP bridge
123	
124	## Device chat turns
125	
126	When a DeskMate device sends `prompt_submit`, the bridge validates its current
127	nonce/epoch, gives the request a single active ACP turn, and calls
128	`session/prompt` with the complete text. It responds with `prompt_ack`, streams
129	sanitized `agent_output` chunks, and ends with `turn_result`. The bridge, its
130	local `deskmate>` REPL, and the device share one turn lock; neither side may
131	interleave prompts in the same ACP session.
132	
133	The bridge does not pass ACP chunks through verbatim. It removes terminal
134	control bytes and obvious inline secrets, batches output for up to 40 ms,
135	splits it at UTF-8 boundaries, and verifies every produced message stays within
136	the 4096-byte link limit. It never waits for an entire answer before streaming.
137	The 2048-byte input limit and 4096-byte wire cap are intentional safety bounds;
138	large document upload is not part of this protocol.

MiMoCode 0.1.14（~/.mimocode/bin/mimo，OpenCode 衍生，agent 名 "OpenCode"）两个关键坑（2026-09-20 实测）：

1. **插件挂死**：`~/.config/mimocode/plugins/` 里放任意外部插件——哪怕只有 `export default {}`——`mimo acp` 就永远不回 initialize（bridge 崩 initialize_timeout，未订阅 MQTT 即死，设备侧看起来就是 "bridge 没跑"）。`--pure` 跳过外部插件即正常。acp-bridge 已改 --pure 启动（选手仓 70798fb），`DESKMATE_MIMO_PURE=0` 可退回。注意 ~/.config/mimocode/plugins/contest-collector.js 本身还是坏的（import ../shared/get_github_login.js 不存在），但挂死与它无关。

# AI Coding 开发日志 — mimo 真后端接入（2026-09-20 下半场）

本文件记录 2026-09-20 下午一轮 AI 主导开发（Claude Code）的真实过程：安装
MiMoCode 并把 acp-bridge 的 mimo 后端从「起进程即崩」打到「设备端真编码
闭环」。三个问题都不在任何一层的报错里——全部靠对比实验与原始报文定位。

## 闭环链路（打通后）

```
qemu 内 ai_agent                      PC（宿主）
  rask <整行指令>                       mosquitto(1883, 本机) + acp-bridge(--backend mimo)
    │ MQTT deskmate/goldfish-1/          │ spawn: mimo acp --pure（外部插件会挂死 initialize）
    │ device-to-bridge                   │ 模型: xiaomi-gw/mimo-v2.5-pro
    ▼                                    ▼（token-plan 网关，Anthropic 兼容 /v1/messages）
  指令全量 JSON ──────────────────> session/prompt → 建文件/跑命令
  [Agent] transcript + 绿 toast <── session/update 流 + transcript 回传
```

## 三个问题（均实测定位）

| # | 现象（零报错） | 根因（实测证据） | 修复 |
|---|----------------|------------------|------|
| 1 | bridge 起 mimo 秒崩 `Error: initialize_timeout` | mimo 0.1.14：`~/.config/mimocode/plugins/` 装**任意外部插件**即永远不回 initialize——空插件 `export default {}` 同样复现（rc=124、stdout 0 字节）；藏起 plugins 目录 / `--pure` / 隔离 MIMOCODE_HOME 三者任一即恢复（433 B 正常回包） | acp-bridge mimo 后端改 `--pure` 启动，`DESKMATE_MIMO_PURE=0` 可退回（选手仓 70798fb，与仓库自带 stdio-verifier 的默认一致） |
| 2 | `session/prompt` 秒回 `end_turn`，0 tokens，无任何报错 | 本机 mimo 未登录（`mimo providers whoami` = Not logged in, 0 credentials）；模型从未被调用。配好自定义 provider 后又踩第二坑：`@ai-sdk/anthropic` 自拼 `/messages`，baseURL 少 `/v1` → 网关 404（DEBUG 日志 `AI_APICallError url=…/anthropic/messages statusCode=404`） | `~/.config/mimocode/mimocode.jsonc`（本机私有，不入仓）配 provider `xiaomi-gw`：`@ai-sdk/anthropic` + baseURL `https://token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com/anthropic/v1` + claude-mimo 包装器同款 token；provider id 不能叫 `xiaomi`（与内置 provider 撞名被影子化） |
| 3 | 设备长指令被截成 7 个词（模型收到 `…containing exactly print('hello`，反问"内容呢？"） | CLI `tokenise()` 上限 `MAX_ARGS=8`（含命令名），`rask`/`ask` 重组 argv[1..] 时静默丢词；`memory_write`/`voice_test_speak` 更只取 argv[1] 单词。MQTT 抓包复现实证：≤7 词全量、>7 词恰在第 7 词截断 | `cli_thread` 在 `strtok` 原地切分前捕获整行剩余文本，四个自由文本命令（ask/rask/memory_write/voice_test_speak）改收原始文本（packages/ai_agent d3588b6） |

## 真实运行记录（2026-09-20 17:0x，qemu goldfish + 本机 bridge）

设备端发起（118 字符指令，此前会被截断）：

```
vela> rask create a file named mimo_test.py containing exactly print('hello from mimo bridge'), then run it with python3 and tell me the output
Prompt sent. Use 'rstat' for progress ...
```

MQTT 抓包（mosquitto_sub device-to-bridge）——全量过桥，逐字节无截断：

```
{"v":1,"cmd":"prompt_submit",...,"text":"create a file named mimo_test.py containing exactly print('hello from mimo bridge'), then run it with python3 and tell me the output"}
```

mimo 真实产物（bridge cwd = tools/acp-bridge）：

```
$ cat mimo_test.py
print('hello from mimo bridge')
```

设备端收尾（transcript 回传 + 完成 toast）：

```
[Agent]: Output:

```
hello from mimo bridge
```
```

计费侧：bridge 会话累计 ~110K tokens（本轮 input 16 / output 118 起，缓存读为主）。

## 排查方法（可复用）

- **mimo acp 直连探测**：`{ printf '<initialize JSON>'; sleep N; } | timeout 10 mimo acp`——比经 bridge 快一个数量级；变量拆分（--pure × MIMOCODE_HOME × plugins 目录）三轮定位插件挂死。
- **response-driven ACP 探测脚本**（await initialize → session/new → session/prompt，stderr 全开）：`--print-logs --log-level DEBUG` 才能看到 `AI_APICallError` 与请求体；acp-adapter 把子进程 stderr 整个吞掉，经 bridge 永远看不到。
- **MQTT 原始报文对照**：`mosquitto_sub -t 'deskmate/<id>/device-to-bridge' -v` 抓 prompt_submit 的 text 字段，区分「设备侧截断」与「bridge/模型侧截断」。

- mimo `--pure` 下 claude-import 仍会同步本机 Claude Code 的 MCP 配置（如 mi-feishu），bridge 会话里可见其工具，属预期行为。

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Redact credentials from AI-session jsonl logs before they are committed.

Patterns and assembled fragments only — no full secret literals in this file.
Writes reuse the same inode (open('w')) so a live appender keeps working.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys

HOME = os.path.expanduser("~")

def mimo_token():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(HOME, ".claude/settings.mimo.json")) as f:
            return json.load(f)["env"]["ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"]
    except Exception:
        return None

# (regex-or-string, replacement, label)
SUBS = [
    (re.compile(r"NjYxNzc1MzY0MjU0Oj[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+"), "<REDACTED:jira-pat>", "jira-pat"),
    (re.compile(r"mcp_u-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{30,}"), "<REDACTED:gerrit-mcp-token>", "gerrit-mcp"),
    ("-".join(["<REDACTED:volc>", "8cbe", "4ef6", "9a18", "<REDACTED:volc>"]), "<REDACTED:volc-key>", "volc-key"),
    ("a2UJdV" + "IuvausiDTp", "<REDACTED:emulator-console-token>", "emu-token"),
    (re.compile(r"ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}"), "<REDACTED:github-token>", "github"),
    ("zy" + "236975", "<REDACTED:sudo-pw>", "sudo-pw"),
    ("deskmate/<REDACTED:mqtt-pw>", "deskmate/<REDACTED:mqtt-pw>", "mqtt-pw-1"),
    (re.compile(r"MQTT_PASSWORD=<REDACTED:mqtt-pw>"), "MQTT_PASSWORD=<REDACTED:mqtt-pw>", "mqtt-pw-2"),
]
m = mimo_token()
if m:
    SUBS.append((m, "<REDACTED:mimo-gw-token>", "mimo-gw-token"))

total = {}
for path in sys.argv[1:]:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
        s = f.read()
    counts = {}
    for pat, rep, label in SUBS:
        if hasattr(pat, "subn"):
            s, n = pat.subn(rep, s)
        else:
            n = s.count(pat)
            s = s.replace(pat, rep)
        if n:
            counts[label] = n
    if counts:
        # Same inode: an O_APPEND writer on this path keeps appending fine.
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(s)
    total[os.path.basename(path)] = counts

print(json.dumps(total, indent=1))

5	created: 2026-09-17
6	description: Use when explaining source code or a technical mechanism as diagram-first Feishu documentation — fenced ASCII text-sketches whose every node/label is grounded in read source (file:line), minimal prose, no slang — and when iteratively refining individual blocks on feedback like "再形象化 / 去俚语 / 减字 / 举个例子 / 具体点". Composes diagram-first-documentation (what to draw) and feishu-document-formatting (how to write safely).
7	---
8	
9	# Code-grounded Visual Docs
10	
11	## Core principle
12	
13	Explain how real code behaves as **diagram-first** content, where every box, edge, branch label, threshold, and cited symbol is copied from source you actually read (with `file:line`), never guessed. Prose is the exception, not the default: prefer a fenced ASCII text-sketch, a small worked numeric example, or a compact table over any paragraph. Write into Feishu one smallest-complete-block at a time, and treat each user reply ("再形象化 / 去俚语 / 减字 / 举例 / 更细") as a scoped rewrite of exactly one block, verified by read-back.
14	
15	This skill is the orchestrator. It does not restate its siblings:
16	- **What to draw / diagram philosophy** → `diagram-first-documentation` (reader questions, fact/interpretation/limit classes, Mermaid-vs-text-sketch selection, terminology ladder, proportional budget).
17	- **How to mutate Feishu safely** → `feishu-document-formatting` (structural manifest, table widths, doc-order mutation, async completion, read-back barrier).
18	
19	Its unique contribution: **code grounding**, the **code-explanation patterns**, the **iterative block-refinement loop**, and the **edit-safety lessons** below.
20	
21	## Non-negotiables
22	
23	- **A diagram reads as authoritative.** A hand-wavy label ("size ok?", "备料", "大概") is a defect. Read the source first; label with the exact identifier or mark it unknown/interpretation.
24	- **No slang, no vague metaphor.** Ban role/action metaphors (登记员, 备料, 兜底, 命脉, 号码牌, 便宜保险). Use the precise term (请求 scratch 的函数, 计算并申请, 回退, ...). Keep standard technical terms (in-place/就地, clamp/夹取, pad/补零, broadcast/广播). Concrete rejected→accepted pairs: `references/anti-examples.md`.
25	- **Minimal text.** Replace paragraphs with a diagram, a table, or a worked example. Each diagram gets at most one one-line takeaway.
26	- **Fenced ASCII text-sketches**, not Mermaid images, when the reader needs precise inline annotation, parallel-lane/SIMD/memory layout, an AND-intersection funnel, a decision fork, a subset relation, or copy-pasteable monospace.
27	
28	## Workflow
29	
30	### 1. Ground in source before drawing
31	
32	Locate the exact code with grep/read (whole files preferred). Record for each claim the `file:line` and the exact identifier. Resolve every intended branch/threshold to source: e.g. a "capability gate" must list the real conditions; a "returns nullptr" must be traced (index out of range → `GetTensorIndex` returns -1). When authorship or intent matters, use `git blame` / `git show` and state fact vs "疑似笔误 (interpretation)". When a claim depends on data (e.g. "quantized bias is 1-D"), verify against a real artifact (inspect the model, run a compile check) rather than asserting from convention.
33	
34	### 2. Pick the encoding by information shape
35	
36	See `references/ascii-diagram-patterns.md` for the reusable catalog: dispatch/flow, AND-gate funnel, binary decision fork, two-gate subset (`{过门2} ⊆ {过门1}`), region/arena layout, ownership two-column, matrix/vector & broadcast worked example, terminology quick-reference (原语速查), and **code-snippet + one-line annotation** (quote the real loop/statement, annotate the one line that matters). Use a table only for exact parallel values or mappings; a table that actually encodes order/causality/layout is a signal to convert it to a sketch.
37	
38	### 3. Structure a code explanation as: 原语 → 判定/流程 → 数字演示
39	
40	When explaining code to a newcomer, layer it:
41	1. **原语速查 (primitives first):** draw each unfamiliar type/macro/function as a mini-sketch (enum→value table; `node->inputs` as an indexed array; a validation macro as `cond? pass : return err`), before the logic that uses it.
42	2. **判定/流程 (decision/flow):** the actual control flow built from those primitives (funnel / fork / two-gate).
43	3. **数字演示 (worked example):** run concrete numbers through it (e.g. `out_c0 = (1+0−3)+10 = 8`; a `[1,2,2,3] + [10,20,30]` broadcast expanded per channel plane). Numbers make "why" land where a formula does not.
44	
45	### 4. Write into Feishu, smallest block first
46	
47	Follow `feishu-document-formatting`. For a new doc use `create_doc`; to extend/repair use `update_doc` with a mode (`append` / `insert_before|after` / `replace_range` / `delete_range`), never `overwrite`/`replace_all` on an existing doc. Put ASCII diagrams inside ` ```plaintext ` fences; angle brackets are safe inside fences (but Feishu table cells eat `<...>` — avoid them in cells). Tables: `lark-table` with `{align="center"}` sets horizontal centering only; vertical centering is a UI action, never claim it from a write.
48	
49	### 5. Refine one block per reply
50	
51	Each feedback ("再形象化 / 去俚语 / 减字 / 举例 / 更细 / 用真实代码不要写无代码") targets one block. Locate it, `replace_range` **only that block's inner text** (keep the ` ``` ` fences), then read back. Escalate/downscale on request: "更细" → add a 原语速查 layer or a worked example; "减字" → collapse prose into a sketch; "用真实代码" → quote the actual source loop instead of describing it. When you correct a prior claim (e.g. "无代码" → "有代码，就是这段循环"), say what changed and why.
52	
53	### 6. Edit-safety (learned the hard way — see `references/edit-and-refine-loop.md`)
54	
55	- **Sequential, never parallel**, when mutating the same document. Parallel `update_doc` calls race and leave duplicated blocks ("Old content deletion failed ... duplicated content").
56	- **`selection_with_ellipsis` `...` collides with literal `...` in code** (`foo(...)`). Anchor on substrings without `...`, or escape as `\.\.\.`.
57	- **Read back after every edit** (`fetch_doc` with a `searchPhrase`): confirm balanced fences, no orphan `lark-*` tags, neighbors intact. MCP success ≠ rendered.
58	- **Concurrent human edits happen.** If a prior insertion vanished or lengths swing between fetches, the user is editing live; re-fetch, confirm stability, and stage around their blocks instead of clobbering.
59	
60	### 7. When the doc drives a code change
61	
62	If the discussion concludes in an actual source edit, keep doc and code honest: apply the edit, **compile-check** (`g++ -fsyntax-only` with the right `-D`/`-I`), verify behavior implications against a real artifact, and — for gerrit — isolate with `git worktree` on the change's current patchset base (so `refs/for/<branch>` does not drag unrelated ancestor commits), stage only the intended file, `--amend`, push. Flag behavior changes and the verification you could not run locally.
63	
64	## Hard rules
65	
66	- No un-grounded node/edge/label; no invented condition or threshold in a diagram.
67	- No slang/metaphor; no paragraph where a sketch/table/example fits.
68	- No Mermaid image when precise inline annotation or copy-pasteable monospace is required.
69	- No `overwrite`/`replace_all` on an existing doc; no parallel writes to one doc.
70	- No `...` inside an ellipsis anchor that also appears literally in the target.
71	- No claim of vertical centering, rendering, or code correctness from a write/MCP acceptance alone — read back, and for code, compile/verify.
72	
73	## Final gate
74	
75	Re-fetch the touched blocks and confirm: every diagram label traces to `file:line` or is marked interpretation/unknown; no slang; prose is minimal and each diagram carries at most one takeaway; fences balanced and no orphan table tags; tables centered horizontally only (vertical centering noted as UI-only). Scan the result against `references/anti-examples.md` — if any block matches a ❌ (metaphor label, prose-where-a-figure-fits, "无代码", 泛泛谈, 是什么/为什么 split, reflexive agreement to an imprecise claim, answer built on the user's misconception), convert it before delivering. State any claim you could not verify (rendered appearance, on-device/functional behavior) as a limit.
76

8	
9	# Feishu Document Formatting
10	
11	## Core contract
12	
13	Format by visible content and semantic role, then mutate the **smallest complete structural block** in document order. An MCP success response is not completion; each completed mutation batch must survive read-back with tables, code, diagrams, media, and neighbors intact.
14	
15	User-explicit styling overrides defaults. Content skills decide facts; this skill controls serialization, layout, update safety, and verification.
16	
17	## Required reference
18	
19	Read [formatting rules](references/formatting-rules.md) before every write.
20	
21	## Workflow
22	
23	### 1. Fetch and classify
24	
25	Choose create, append/insert, restyle one block, replace one section, or repair malformed rich text. For an existing document, call `fetch_doc` without `limit`/`offset` to get the complete document, then locate boundaries locally. Use pagination only when the user explicitly requests it; in that case continue until the complete target block and both neighbors are available. Never infer current headings/tokens from an old draft.
26	
27	### 2. Build the structural manifest
28	
29	In document order record headings; table boundaries/shape; fenced code and Mermaid boundaries; callout/grid/container boundaries; whiteboard/image/file tokens, order, and neighbors; and target/preserve status. Do not split a table/fence/container or cross unrelated media.
30	
31	### 3. Allocate auditable widths
32	
33	Table total width matches the document's **actual text-column width**, verified so it does not overflow the adjacent callout/heading: wide-mode docs ≈ 930px, classic/narrow docs ≈ 800px. Width count equals column count and width sum equals the chosen total.
34	
35	- tiny enum/index: 70–100;
36	- status/date/version: 90–140;
37	- numeric before/after/delta: 105–145;
38	- symbol/API: 150–220;
39	- repo/code path/revision: 210–300;
40	- explanation/evidence/root cause: remaining 280–500.
41	
42	Center headers and compact values; for a user-requested uniform-centered style, center **all** cells with equal columns summing to the text width. Leave paths/prose left-aligned by omitting `align`. Vertical centering (垂直居中) is not settable via the update tool — it is a Feishu UI action (select table → 垂直居中); never claim it from a write. If the text width is insufficient for readability, split by question.
43	
44	### 4. Preflight serialization
45	
46	Check canonical same-block bold; alignment outside emphasis; balanced table/row/cell structure; equal cell count per row; balanced code/Mermaid fences; blank-line separation; container support; and punctuation locale consistency (CJK context → full-width marks, pure-ASCII context → ASCII mark + space, no mixing, code/ASCII fences exempt). Fenced code in an enhanced table cell is allowed only when its complete nested syntax has been intentionally validated; Mermaid/media/nested tables are not inserted into cells. Never write a fetched `<whiteboard token="..."/>` as creation syntax.
47	
48	### 5. Mutate in document order
49	
50	Policy for existing documents: no `overwrite` or `replace_all`. Use one unique complete-block `replace_range`; `selection_by_title` only for the exact fetched section; precise insert modes for adjacency; append only at the true end. If `selection_with_ellipsis` includes literal `...`, escape it as `\.\.\.`. Process the earliest remaining target first; one section per batch is the long-report default.
51	
52	### 6. Resolve asynchronous completion
53	
54	A mutation returning `task_id` is not a completed batch. Poll the same create/update tool with `task_id` until success/failure. Only then fetch and validate. Never begin another mutation while the preceding batch is pending.
55	
56	### 7. Enforce the read-back barrier
57	
58	After every completed batch, fetch the affected complete block and neighbors. Verify content/order; table shape/width count/sum; alignment; bold; code/Mermaid fences/language/order; container boundaries; media token/order/neighbors; warnings; and unrelated content. On failure, stop and repair only the smallest failed block, then re-run the barrier.
59	
60	## Hard rules
61	
62	- No existing-document `overwrite`/`replace_all` under this safety policy.
63	- No non-unique selection or speculative broadening.
64	- No split structural block or unrelated media crossing.
65	- No table width that overflows the document text column; match the verified text-column width (≈800 narrow, ≈930 wide).
66	- No claim that vertical centering was applied via a write (it is UI-only).
67	- No width-count/sum mismatch.
68	- No blanket centering of paths/prose.
69	- No mixed punctuation locales: CJK-context punctuation is full-width, pure-ASCII-context punctuation is ASCII + space; applies to all marks, never inside code/ASCII fences.
70	- No next batch before async completion and read-back pass.
71	- No rendering-success claim from MCP acceptance alone.
72	
73	## Final gate
74	
75	After all batch barriers, full-fetch and compare the initial manifest plus intended changes. Confirm headings, tables, fences, links, containers, media/neighbors, and warnings. Markdown read-back does not by itself prove visual font weight or final bitmap rendering; state that limit.
76

4	version: "1.0"
5	created: 2026-08-20
6	description: Use when turning fragmented engineering notes, diffs, logs, measurements, or existing documents into newcomer-readable technical documentation for code review, debugging or incident review, implementation walkthroughs, feature handoff, validation closure, or technical decisions.
7	---
8	
9	# Diagram-first Documentation
10	
11	## Core principle
12	
13	Organize around the reader's questions, not the author's chronology. Use diagrams only where they compress structure or causality better than prose, while keeping every claim tied to evidence.
14	
15	**Two task shapes.** (a) Author a new document from raw notes/diffs/logs. (b) **Convert** an existing document's flat prose or tables into diagrams on request (e.g. "文字不生动，绘制图形表示原理和流程"). In conversion mode: preserve the existing facts, exact labels, and neighbouring rich content; change only the targeted block into the visual that fits its information shape (see the two-step encoding decision in diagram-selection); add at most one takeaway; and do not let the new diagram duplicate an adjacent one.
16	
17	**A diagram reads as authoritative, so precision matters more than in prose.** Never let a visual encode a vague, guessed, or unverified condition, threshold, or step—a hand-wavy branch label such as "size ok?" is a defect, not decoration. Every node, edge, and label must be copied from evidence, derived from it and marked as interpretation, or shown as unknown. Converting prose into a picture must not smuggle in a fact the evidence does not state; if a real condition is fuzzy, make it precise from the source (e.g. "compile-time flag on?") or mark it unknown.
18	
19	## Workflow
20	
21	### 1. Fix the goal and scope
22	
23	Identify the audience, review goal, supplied evidence, desired output, and publication target. If a missing audience or goal would materially change the document, ask one focused question; otherwise assume a technical newcomer preparing to review.
24	
25	Do not add operations, hardening, ownership, rationale, tests, or lifecycle behavior absent from the inputs, and do not expand the result into full API or source documentation. Include unsupported ideas only when the user requests recommendations or an unresolved decision requires them; then keep them in a short **Follow-up** section labeled as proposals.
26	
27	### 2. Inventory evidence
28	
29	Classify important statements before drafting:
30	
31	| Class | Use for |
32	|---|---|
33	| **Fact** | Direct observations from source, diffs, logs, measurements, or document content |
34	| **Interpretation** | Explanations supported by facts but not raw evidence |
35	| **Decision** | Chosen action, trade-off, or review conclusion |
36	| **Limit** | Unknown, untested path, or boundary beyond which the conclusion does not apply |
37	
38	Never smooth uncertainty into fact. Keep rejected hypotheses distinguishable from the supported explanation.
39	
40	### 3. Map reader questions and classify source complexity
41	
42	Select only questions that serve the stated goal, in this order when relevant:
43	
44	1. What happened or changed?
45	2. Where is it in the larger system?
46	3. How does the important mechanism work?
47	4. What changed, and what deliberately stayed unchanged?
48	5. What evidence supports the conclusion?
49	6. What remains unknown or outside scope?
50	7. What decision or next action follows?
51	
52	Each section and diagram must answer one of these questions. Remove material that answers none.
53	
54	Before drafting, build an internal coverage map for every selected question:
55	
56	```text
57	reader question → supporting evidence → best visual → exact-value table, if needed → limiting evidence
58	```
59	
60	Classify the input by **independent information layers**, not raw length:
61	
62	- **Short or single-mechanism note:** one main chain plus a compact proof or boundary. Use the concise path.
63	- **Long or multi-stage handoff:** several distinct layers—such as system position, transformation stages, before/after structure, performance or memory causality, experiment isolation, and validation closure—where collapsing a layer would break traceability. Use the deep handoff path.
64	
65	When a long engineering source is requested as a document “for others” or for newcomers and no narrower goal is supplied, default to a newcomer-readable **technical handoff**, not an executive summary. Do not mistake a concise prompt for a request to discard supplied technical layers.
66	
67	### 4. Build the terminology ladder before technical wording
68	
69	Introduce specialized concepts as:
70	
71	```text
72	plain-language meaning → technical term → exact source/code label
73	```
74	
75	Example: `two read positions → input cursors → pa / pb`.
76	
77	Use a plain-language title and opening where possible. For a Chinese long-form deep technical document, name the deliverable with **“深度梳理”**—for example, `主题：机制、部署与性能归因深度梳理`. Do not use **“交接”** or **“技术交接”** in the document title; keep `handoff` only as an internal workflow classification, not reader-facing naming. If the user explicitly supplies a title, preserve it unless they ask for renaming. If the conclusion needs an unfamiliar term, place the terminology key immediately after the title and before the conclusion. Expand every acronym at its first appearance, including conclusions, tables, and diagram labels. Put the key before the first technical sentence or visual that depends on unfamiliar protocol, metric, operation, or component terms; include all nouns used by the first diagram, not only acronyms.
78	
79	After drafting, scan from the first line downward and verify that each specialized term is defined before that occurrence. Keep exact function, field, event, instruction, and file names for deep review, but make the plain-language meaning primary. Add a legend only when colors, line styles, symbols, or abbreviations carry meaning.
80	
81	### 5. Choose one evidence-backed visual per question
82	
83	Read [references/diagram-selection.md](references/diagram-selection.md) for type selection, complexity-sensitive visual budgets, density, legends, and generic Mermaid **and plaintext text-sketch** patterns.
84	
85	**Two visual encodings are equally canonical**: rendered diagrams (Mermaid) and inline **plaintext text-sketches** — ASCII box/arrow/lane drawings inside a fenced code block. When a principle or flow is currently written as prose or a plain table and reads as "not vivid" (文字不生动), convert it to a diagram rather than leaving it as text: use **Mermaid** for flow/sequence/state that benefits from rendering, and a **text-sketch** when you need precise inline annotations, parallel-lane / SIMD layout, memory/buffer layout, an AND-intersection funnel, a compact state machine, or role/ownership labels running alongside the flow — or when platform rendering is unreliable and you want copy-pasteable monospace. A table stays a table only for exact parallel values or mappings; a table that actually encodes order, causality, transformation, or layout is a signal to convert it.
86	
87	- For a short or single-mechanism note, use **1–3 core diagrams** according to distinct evidence-backed questions; one diagram is enough when the source supports only one visual question.
88	- For a long or multi-stage handoff, let distinct reader questions determine the count; **4–7 non-duplicative diagrams is typical, not a quota**. Keep up to the first 2–3 in the one-minute path and place supporting proof, attribution, decision, or validation visuals in deep review.
89	- Do not convert a process, causal chain, transformation, experiment-isolation boundary, decision path, or validation loop into a table merely because earlier diagrams already consumed a numeric budget. Use tables for exact comparisons, mappings, and compact evidence lookup.
90	
91	Give each mechanism or causal chain one canonical visual. For a system interaction or feature handoff, the primary interaction diagram must span every participant named in the requested scope, including asynchronous consumers and delivery components. A secondary diagram is justified only when it answers a different reader question, such as lifecycle failure, resource causality, comparison validity, or proof closure. Do not pair a sequence diagram and flowchart for the same chain.
92	
93	Preserve the evidence-backed **intermediate states** required to understand a conclusion. If a conclusion depends on several transformations or causal steps, a start→end summary is insufficient; show those steps or mark the unavailable link as unknown. Split crowded visuals by reader question instead of deleting the states that carry the explanation.
94	
95	Each node, edge, destination, responsibility, and edge label must be copied from the input or clearly labeled as interpretation. Do not enrich a request with likely payload details or insert a likely event channel. If a destination or owner is unknown, show the boundary as unknown or omit it.
96	
97	Add at most one takeaway after a diagram, and only when it contributes information the labels alone do not provide. Omit it when the labels already carry the point.
98	
99	### 6. Compose to a proportional reading budget
100	
101	- **10 seconds:** title and one-sentence conclusion or purpose.
102	- **1 minute:** up to the first 2–3 core diagrams, each with at most one useful takeaway, plus an explicit change/result boundary.
103	- **Deep review:** additional distinct visuals, source map, exact evidence, commands or values, decisions, and limits.
104	
105	For short source notes, impose **no word-count or diagram minimum**. Use **1–3 diagrams** according to the evidence-backed questions, and keep a **900-word ceiling** unless the user requested depth or omission would lose supplied evidence. Evidence-rich short notes commonly land around **600–850 words**, but tiny one-question inputs should remain substantially shorter. Remove repeated takeaways, generic cautions, undefined side concepts, and redundant checklists first.
106	
107	For long or multi-stage handoffs, do **not** impose the short-note word or diagram ceiling. Keep the one-minute path independently scannable, then spend deep-review space in proportion to the independent questions and supplied evidence. Added length must come from useful visual layers, exact evidence, boundaries, or decisions—not arrow-by-arrow narration, repeated conclusions, or prose padding. In a process-heavy handoff, diagrams should normally be at least as numerous as tables; treat a table-heavy draft as a signal to re-check whether a process or causal chain was flattened into rows.
108	
109	Useful default shapes are:
110	
111	```text
112	Short note:
113	Plain-language title → terminology → conclusion → 1–3 evidence-backed core visuals → evidence and limits
114	
115	Long handoff:
116	Plain-language title → terminology → one-minute visual path → deep mechanism/transformation visuals
117	→ exact comparison tables → attribution and experiment boundaries → validation closure and limits
118	```
119	
120	Treat each important point and quantitative value as having one primary home. After the canonical causal visual, do not add an “at a glance” chronology that walks the arrows again. An evidence table should map claims to evidence, not reconstruct the sequence. A key boundary may appear in the conclusion, one diagram, and one evidence or limit statement; do not restate it in every takeaway, checklist, and section.
121	
122	### 7. Produce the canonical document first
123	
124	Write platform-neutral Markdown. The canonical visual source is Mermaid for rendered diagrams and fenced plaintext text-sketches (ASCII) for inline principle/flow drawings; both are platform-neutral and survive without an image round-trip. Separate product behavior, measurement instrumentation, and validation assets whenever they coexist; state only the supplied role and do not infer deployment or shipping status from a test or profile path.
125	
126	Preserve source ambiguity instead of resolving it. Do not infer that one branch ran merely because another did not, convert a tested dimension into a supported boundary, or complete missing ownership and data destinations from typical architecture. Attribute conclusions to the evidence that directly proves them—for example, a byte comparison proves byte identity while a matching hash only corroborates it.
127	
128	Use the source's exact metric name and scope: `502 rate = 0` does not become “failure rate = 0.” Avoid comparative claims such as “smallest,” “only,” or “all” unless the supplied evidence establishes the comparison set. Do not infer behavior of successful or unobserved cases from an intermittent failure description.
129	
130	Do not add claims about rendering, deployment, authorization, ownership, unchanged responsibilities, verification steps, request contents, or data destinations unless they were actually checked or supplied. Label necessary interpretation as interpretation.
131	
132	Only adapt or publish to Feishu when requested. Before doing so, read [references/feishu-adapter.md](references/feishu-adapter.md). Default to draft and preview, not silent publication.
133	
134	## Final gate
135	
136	Before delivery, apply every objective gate in [references/readability-gates.md](references/readability-gates.md). Revise failed gates rather than hiding them with more prose; if a gate cannot be verified, state the corresponding limit.
137

1	# PC 侧 MCP server（remote_ctrl + vela 编译）
2	
3	跑在 PC（宿主机）上的 MCP server，供设备端 ai_agent（mcp_client）经 HTTP 调用。
4	一次 `mcp_add` 同时拿到两组能力：
5	
6	| 组 | 工具 | 用途 |
7	|----|------|------|
8	| 远程编码 | `rc_repo_open` / `rc_read_file` / `rc_write_patch` / `rc_run` / `rc_git`（push 禁用）/ `rc_summary` | 在 PC 仓库上读改跑提交（配合 mimocode / ACP bridge 的编码闭环） |
9	| vela 编译 | `vela_build` / `vela_build_status` | 在 PC 上发起 vela 固件编译并轮询结果 |
10	
11	设备端 ai_agent 只发起与查询，编译产物和日志都留在 PC，不占用设备上下文与存储。
12	
13	## 启动
14	
15	```bash
16	cd <openvela workspace 根目录>
17	python3 packages/ai_agent/pc/remote_ctrl_mcp_server.py \
18	    --root . --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8760
19	# 可选: --token <secret>           # 开启 x-user-token 鉴权
20	# 可选: --jobs 32                  # vela_build 默认 -j
21	# 可选: --log-dir /tmp             # 编译日志目录
22	# 可选: --target bk7258-devkit-ap=vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/ap
23	#       （--target NAME=CONFIG_PATH 可重复传，扩展白名单）
24	```
25	
26	内置 target 白名单：`goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap`、`qemu-arm64-v8a-ap`（映射到
27	`vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/<target>`）。白名单外的 target 一律拒绝。
28	
29	## 设备端接入（qemu）
30	
31	qemu guest 经 `10.0.2.2` 访问宿主。在 ai_agent CLI 中：
32	
33	```
34	mcp_add pc http://10.0.2.2:8760/mcp
35	mcp_discover
36	```
37	
38	配置持久化在 config store（`ai.mcp.server.<idx>.*`），重启后仍在。
39	
40	设备端「编译 vela」skill（`agent_skills/vela-build.md`，随固件 builtin 分发）
41	会引导 agent 完成上述配置和调用。
42	
43	## 为什么 vela_build 是异步的
44	
45	设备侧 HTTP 读超时 = `AGENT_LLM_SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SEC` = 120 s，而 vela 编译
46	增量 ~35 s、clean 要几分钟——同步等待必然超时。所以：
47	
48	```
49	ai_agent                    PC server
50	   │ vela_build {target}       │  校验白名单 → 起后台线程 → <1s 返回 started
51	   │──────────────────────────>│
52	   │<──────────────────────────│
53	   │ vela_build_status {}      │  （线程内: unset CROSSDEV; source build/envsetup.sh
54	   │──────────────────────────>│    && lunch <config> && m -jN，日志落 --log-dir）
55	   │<── running / success / …  │
56	   │  …每 30–60 s 轮询…        │
57	```
58	
59	`vela_build_status` 返回 `state`（idle|running|success|failed）、`target`、`elapsed`；
60	失败时附 `return code` 与 `log_tail`（末 ~2.5 KB，定位错误行），成功时附 artifact
61	（`out/openvela_vela_<target>/vela_ap.bin` 等）。running 态回复保持一行（不带
62	log_tail）——agent 反复轮询时不会撑爆自身上下文。
63	
64	`vela_build_status {"wait": 60}`：server 端阻塞最长 90 s（须低于设备 120 s 读超时），
65	state 离开 running 即刻返回。LLM 自己无法在轮次间等待，`wait` 是它控制轮询节奏的
66	唯一手段——skill 里就是这么教的。
67	
68	## 安全模型
69	
70	- **路径 confinement**：所有 rc_* 路径解析后必须落在 `--root` 内，逃逸（`../`）拒绝。
71	- **命令 allowlist**：`rc_run` 只允许白名单首 token（python3/pip/pytest/make/gcc/…），
72	  `shell=False` 逐参数执行，无管道/`&&`，带超时。
73	- **编译命令由 server 拼装**：`vela_build` 只接受 target 名（白名单校验），
74	  `lunch` 的 config 路径来自 server 端 target 表，agent 无法注入任意 shell。
75	- **push 禁用**：`rc_git` 不提供 push，推送走 Gerrit MCP（人工 review）。
76	- **可选 token**：`--token` 开启后所有请求须带 `x-user-token`。
77	- **同时只允许一个 build**：running 期间再次 `vela_build` 直接拒绝并提示轮询。
78	
79	## 测试
80	
81	```bash
82	# 起一个假 workspace + server
83	python3 pc/test_mcp.py                       # 需先起 server（见脚本头部注释）
84	```

86	`test_mcp.py` 覆盖：initialize/tools/list、rc_* 全套、allowlist 拦截（`rm`）、
87	路径逃逸拒绝、push 拒绝，以及 vela_build/status 的假构建全流程
88	（假 root + 假 build 脚本，不真编）。
89	
90	## 已知边界
91	
92	- server 单进程内共享一个 build 槽位（全局锁），多设备同时编同一 PC 会互相拒绝。
93	- 编译产物留在 PC 的 `out/openvela_vela_<target>/`，设备端只读状态文本。
94	- `log_tail` 截 2.5 KB，若需完整日志直接看 `--log-dir` 下的 `vela_build_<target>_<时间戳>.log`。
95	
96	## BK7258 板上 media 框架可行性（spike 实测，结论 no-go）
97	
98	2026-09-20 实测（ap defconfig 加 `CONFIG_MEDIA=y CONFIG_MEDIA_SERVER=y`
99	（含 `NET/NET_LOCAL/EVENT_FD` 依赖）→ full_flow 构建）：
100	
101	- **基线**：AP `app1.bin` 336,852 B（XIP 分区 2.78 MB，余 2.58 MB），RAM
102	  336 KB 仅驻留 data+bss 12.5 KB；工具链 armv8-m.main / cortex-m33 soft-float。
103	- **`CONFIG_MEDIA_SERVER=y` 构建失败**：`server/media_plugin.c:3` 无条件
104	  `#include <libavutil/mem.h>`（`av_mallocz/av_freep` 是所有 plugin 的私数据
105	  分配路径）；`audio_graph.c`/`media_player.c`/`media_recorder.c` 同样直接
106	  依赖 libav*。本树无 ARMv8-M ffmpeg（prebuilts 只有 A64/x86），移植亦受
107	  2.78 MB XIP 分区与 M33 soft-float 限制 —— **media server 本身编不过，
108	  不是体积问题**。
109	- **退到 `CONFIG_MEDIA=y`（仅 client 库）也失败**：`utils/media_utils.c:25`
110	  `#include <cutils/properties.h>` —— client 依赖 Android 风格 property 服务
111	  基础设施，AP 镜像没有；且无 server 时 client 编过也是死代码
112	  （`media_player_open` 连不上 → audio_playback 回退 NUTTX direct）。
113	- **结论 no-go**：板侧 `/dev/audio/pcm0p`、`pcm0c` 是标准 NuttX audio
114	  lower-half（media graph 经 aw-alsa-lib 消费的正是这类设备），但 mediad +
115	  ffmpeg filter graph（alsasrc/alsasink）需要 A 核/PSRAM 级资源。板上音频
116	  维持 NuttX audio 框架；media 框架链路由 qemu（goldfish，media-only
117	  播放+采集）承载。
118	- defconfig 已还原，复原构建 `decode pass`，镜像与基线逐字节一致。

Application Configuration → Packages → Vela AI Agent → Enable Feishu bot channel

1	# Vela Build
2	
3	Compile vela firmware on the PC via the `pc` MCP server, and report progress and result.
4	
5	## When to use
6	When user asks to:
7	- 编译固件 / 编译 vela / build the firmware
8	- 查看编译进度或结果（编译好了吗）
9	- clean 全量重编
10	
11	## How to use
12	
13	### 1. Ensure the pc server is connected
14	- `mcp_status` — check a server named `pc` is present and connected
15	- If missing (first use only, config is persisted):
16	  - `run_shell "mcp_add pc http://10.0.2.2:8760/mcp"`
17	  - `run_shell "mcp_discover"`
18	
19	### 2. Start the build (async!)
20	- `pc.vela_build {"target": "goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap", "clean": false}`
21	- target defaults to `goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap`; `clean: true` = full rebuild (much slower)
22	- Returns `started` immediately — do NOT wait for the build in this call.
23	  The build runs on the PC; a single HTTP request would time out at 120 s.
24	
25	### 3. Poll status (with server-side wait)
26	- `pc.vela_build_status {"wait": 60}`
27	- `wait` holds the call up to 60 s while the build runs, then returns the
28	  current state — repeat until terminal. Never poll in a tight loop: the
29	  running-state reply is small, but each round trip costs an LLM turn.
30	- `state: running` → call `vela_build_status {"wait": 60}` again
31	- `state: success` → report artifact (e.g. vela_ap.bin + size) and elapsed time
32	- `state: failed` → report the error lines from `log_tail`
33	
34	The PC keeps the full log; `log_tail` (last ~2.5 KB) is only included on
35	failure — the running-state reply is a one-liner by design.
36	
37	## Limits
38	- Only one build at a time on the PC (a second `vela_build` while running is rejected)
39	- Build output stays on the PC under `out/openvela_vela_<target>/`
40

## 6. AI 执行操作约定（本节给执行 AI，防止现场摸索）

1. **输入**：`printf '%s\n' "<命令>" > /tmp/qin`（fifo 保持打开由 qemu 持有；不要 cat > /tmp/qin 交互式挂住）。
2. **读输出**：`tail -n 50 /tmp/qemu_stdio.log`；等待某输出用轮询（`for i in $(seq 1 30); do grep -q "<标志>" /tmp/qemu_stdio.log && break; sleep 2; done`），超时即按场景的「失败处置」走。
3. **节奏**：一条命令等回显/结果再发下一条；LLM 场景给足 30–60 s。
4. **严禁**：`kill -9` qemu（FAT 孤儿簇根因）；`Ctrl+C` 交给用户；Mify key 明文出现在任何输出。
5. **每场景结束**：记录「场景号 / 通过与否 / 实际耗时 / 异常」，最后汇总成验收表（见第 8 节格式）。
6. **预检轮发现失败**：先排障重试一次；仍失败 → 记录并在录制轮跳过该场景，不要卡死整个流程。

## 7. 风险与处置速查

| 症状 | 根因 | 处置 |
|------|------|------|
| rstat 长期 Offline | bridge 未起 / mimo 挂 | `tail /tmp/mimo_bridge.log`；有 `initialize_timeout` → 重启 bridge（3.4） |
| TTS 报 -EIO 写文件失败 | /data FAT 满 | 停 qemu → `fsck.fat -a` + 删 `FSCK*.REC` → 重启（3.1/3.6） |
| ask 报 No available backend | set_llm 未配/丢失 | 重跑第 4 节配置块（RAM 态配置，qemu 重启即清） |
| 语音无采音 | HFP 未连/非默认源 | 回 3.2；连不上则 S4 降级为文字演示 |
| 窗口黑屏无 fb0 | 窗口模式 GPU 未挂 | 3.6 的 `-qemu -device virtio-gpu-device` fallback |
| agent 敲错命令后无响应 | cli 线程卡 | 等 10 s；仍卡 → 整机重启流程（停 qemu → 3.1 → 3.6 → 第 4 节重配） |
| jira 工具不在列表 | PAT 吊销 | 跳过 S6，其余照常 |
| vela_build 被拒（已有构建在跑） | 上一轮 build 未终态 | `pc.vela_build_status {}` 等终态后再发起 |

2026-09-20 预演实测：设备 `rask`（remote_agent_prompt）→ MQTT → PC 侧 mimocode 完整执行 Gerrit 补丁修订：读 AGENT_TASK.txt → 改 hello_main.c（新增 sub()）→ gcc 桩编译 → `git commit -a --amend --no-edit`（Change-Id 不变）→ `git push vela HEAD:refs/for/trunk-25rc05` → 同链接新 patchset（10334000 从 PS8 → PS9，e4635fe6a3d5）。mimo 全程逐步播报回设备气泡；`ronce`/`rdeny` 均实测可用。

**Why:** 架构演示的编码腿必须走 mimo（不是设备直连 rc_* 工具）；且权限门有多道（读任务/读文件/写文件/…），每道都要 ronce。

**How to apply:**
1. bridge 必须带 `DESKMATE_PERMISSION_TIMEOUT_MS=300` 启动——bridge-core 默认 30 s 审批超时，到点 `core.disconnect()` 掉链，且**设备侧 remote 通道会 wedge**（set_remote 反复起不来、rstat 一直 "not configured"），唯一恢复 = 停 qemu → fsck → 重启 → 重配（MCP 配置不持久化，全量重加）。修复提交：选手仓 f580ba4（tools/acp-bridge/bin/deskmate-bridge.mjs）。

3. worktree 重建：`git -C ~/project26/vela-miwear-bes-o62-25rc05-tflm/apps worktree add --detach /tmp/apps_hello_wt fa64b10b1cc8`（Gerrit ssh 只许 push 不许 fetch；tflm checkout 里有 PS7 对象）。gcc 桩：`gcc -I/tmp/hello_stub examples/hello/hello_main.c -o /tmp/hello_out`。
4. 设备端 ask/rask 文本上限 ≈256 字节（UTF-8）：超长行被 CLI 静默丢弃（有 echo 无 Sent to agent）——长任务写 AGENT_TASK.txt，ask 用短句指向它。
5. qemu fifo 必须挂常驻写端 `nohup sleep infinity > /tmp/qin &`，否则所有写端关闭 → qemu stdin EOF 秒退；TaskStop emulator 任务杀的是 bash 包装，qemu 本体可能存活，用 `ps aux | grep qemu-system | grep -v grep` 确认。相关 [[goldfish-emulator-console-fifo]]。
